newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 18.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec will meet with his Polish and Hungarian counterparts in Prague today to discuss steps they will take for successful entry into NATO.

- Komercni Banka has not changed its estimate for GDP growth of between 1.5 and 2.5 percent. It estimates a deficit of about one percent of GDP, average inflation of less than 10 percent, unemployment of between 4.5 and 4.8 percent and a trade deficit between 145 and 170 billion crowns, but closer to the higher sum.
- The year-on-year increase in retail sales in May was 3.1 percent, and the increase since the beginning of the year is just above one percent.
- For the first six months of this year, the metal and machine tools company Vitkovice had gross profits of 50 million crowns, compared to losses of 205 million for the first half of last year.

PRAVO - In eastern Bohemia and all of Moravia, citizens are afraid of meteorologists' forecasts that it will rain all weekend. Citizens and the central flood commission are preparing for another disaster. Reports are that so far 46 people have died.

- Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl estimates flood damages in industry, excluding construction and internal trade, at about 25 billion crowns. For internal trade and construction, damages will probably be several hundred million.
- The Czech National Bank proposes the cabinet should consider a short-term increase in income taxes for citizens to obtain more money to help areas affected by the floods.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Finance Ministry announced yesterday that government bonds to help flood relief which will be available from August 1, will have an interest rate in the first year of 12.5 percent and in the following four years, the interest rate will be 2.5 percent higher than yearly inflation.
- Seven candidates have entered the tender for Becherovka. Originally, there were eight potential investors, but one did not fulfill conditions and was excluded, according to the Finance Ministry.
- From today, Banka Hana will decrease its reference rate to 18 percent from 20 percent. Other interest rates for timed accounts will also change.
- The chairman of the Anti-monopoly Office approved entry of French Bongrain into dairy Povltavske Mlekarny Sedlcany. Bongrain must invest 107.5 million crowns in production in the next three years.

- In reaction to farmers' requests to increase prices, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux said prices of agricultural products should increase with their competitiveness, which is 20 to 30 percent lower than in the EU.

- Finance Minister Ivan Pilip yesterday signed a contract with the vice-president of the European Investment Bank for a government grant of 200 million ECU to finance construction of the Czech part of the railway line Warsaw-Ostrava-Vienna.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Most domestic insurance companies have noticed an increase in demand for housing insurance. Many people are trying to insure themselves before another wave of floods hits.
- The city of Prague will give 50 million crowns from its budget to help areas that were affected by the floods.
